IMPLEMENTER_REPORT:
ROUND: 0
STATUS: DONE
SUGGESTION_RESOLUTIONS:
none
SELF_REVIEW:
- AC1 — entry no longer exposes a directory-level resolution status or its reason strings; failure is derived from the skill files the entry owns:
  `ExpectedSetEntry` in crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs no longer has a `resolution` field (its `source_dir` is documented as a location anchor only), `ResolutionStatus` is documented as skill-file-only vocabulary, and `generate_manifest` now skips on `skill.is_failed()` instead of `matches!(skill.resolution, ResolutionStatus::Resolved)`. A `grep` over crates/ and tests/ finds no `entry.resolution` reads; the workspace compiles, which makes such a read impossible. Consumers (`dev`, `pack`, `validation-runner`, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs`) already read `SkillFile.resolution`.
- AC2 — failure messages keep naming the missing location and reason, no wording loss:
  the reason strings produced by the enumerator are unchanged; the vendor/upstream missing-directory tests now assert them exactly (`"vendor skill directory not found: <dir>"`, `"upstream skill directory not found: <dir>"`) on the owned root skill file, rather than the removed entry-level status. `dev` (`missing_skill_files`), `pack` (`reject_failed_entries`), and `validation-runner` (`validate_all`) message code is untouched and their suites pass (deploy 35, validation-runner 34).
- AC3 — compiles, `cargo test --workspace` green, no consumer reads the retired status, clippy clean:
  `cargo test --workspace` → 335 passed, 0 failed across 16 test binaries (skill-index 22, deploy 35, validation-runner 34, distill 113, shared 17, skill-check 24, validation 28, git-utils 4, plus distill integration suites 3/8/15/9/17/1/4/1). `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` exits 0; the only warnings are the pre-existing `unused dependency anyhow` / `unused dependency serde_json` manifest warnings in the `validation` crate, untouched by this change and present before it.
- AC4 — behavior unchanged versus the previous ticket:
  no consumer logic was edited (only the enumerator's data shape and its tests plus two stale comments); dev policy (warn and skip `is_failed()`), pack strictness (fail naming every missing file), tarball/installed layout, lock format, and every entry-state verdict test stay green unchanged. The one latent difference — `generate_manifest` previously would have listed an existing directory whose root `SKILL.md` was absent — is unreachable in the shipped pipeline because `pack` rejects that entry first; the new regression test pins the safe behavior instead.
- AC5 — existing suites referee and stay green without relaxing assertions:
  all pre-existing test bodies still assert the same outcomes; assertions that referenced the retired entry-level status were migrated to the equivalent/stronger skill-file facts (exact reason equality plus `is_failed()`), and the new `generate_manifest_skips_entries_with_a_missing_owned_skill_file` test was written RED first (`panic: an entry with a missing skill file must not invent a manifest entry`) before the implementation change.
- Test quality / mock discipline: the new test exercises the public boundary (`discover_skills` on a real temp tree → `generate_manifest`), no mocks, no sleeps; migrated tests assert through the public `skill_file`/`is_failed` interface.
- Scope creep: none beyond documenting the retired term in CONTEXT.md and rewording two stale "resolution" comments in validation-runner's test module.
- No issues found.

CHANGED_FILES:
- CONTEXT.md — "Expected-set entry" definition now lists identity, Skill source, source-tree location, and owned Skill files; states the entry carries no resolution status of its own and is failed when any owned file is missing.
- crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs — removed `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution`; reworded `ResolutionStatus` docs to skill-file semantics; dropped entry-level initializers in `discover_skills`, `resolved_entry`, `failed_entry`; `generate_manifest` skips with `is_failed()`; migrated enumeration tests and added `generate_manifest_skips_entries_with_a_missing_owned_skill_file`.
- crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs — removed the entry-level `resolution` initializer from the `test_entry` fixture; reworded two stale directory-resolution comments.
- crates/deploy/src/dev.rs (pre-existing) — consumer already derives failure from `entry.is_failed()` / `SkillFile.resolution`; not edited.
- crates/deploy/src/pack.rs (pre-existing) — consumer already names every missing skill file from `entry.skill_files`; not edited.
- tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs (pre-existing) — already reads skill files only; not edited.
- docs/adr/0045-expected-set-entry-resolves-its-skill-files.md (pre-existing) — already records the retirement in its Decision and Consequences; not edited.

SUMMARY: Retired `ExpectedSetEntry`'s directory-level `resolution` status so all Expected-set failure verdicts derive solely from the skill files each entry owns, preserving every consumer's message and behavior, verified by a green 335-test workspace run and a clean clippy.
